Brooklyn Bridge Park  Investment Advisory Services
notices.description: Brooklyn Bridge Park, an eighty-five (85) acre civic waterfront space in Brooklyn, NY, is designed to be both environmentally and financially sustainable. To further diversify its financial resources, Brooklyn Bridge Park seeks to procure investment advisory services. The selected firm will be required to perform services for: Portfolio and asset management; Policy governance and advisory services; Performance monitoring and reporting; Risk management and compliance; Communication and ongoing support. Proposers must be an investment advisor or banking institution registered under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 or registered with the U. S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) or the New York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS). Proposers must also demonstrate compliance with NYPMIFA, NPCL, and all applicable New York State and New York City fiduciary and financial regulations.

notices.short_title: SNAP Outreach to low-income households
notices.vendor_name: Food Bank for New York City
notices.description: The Human Resources Administration (HRA) intends to enter into a Required Source contract with Food Bank for New York City for SNAP Outreach to increase SNAP participation. SNAP Outreach is a 50 percent reimbursement program in which the New York State Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance (OTDA) reimburses approved, reasonable and necessary SNAP Outreach expenditures. The Federal funding is granted with the understanding that this funding supports the implementation of outreach activities to inform low-income households about the availability, eligibility requirements, application procedures and the benefits of SNAP. OTDA funds this Required Source contract and authorizes HRA to contract with Food Bank for New York City. The term of this contract is 10.01.2024 to 9.30.2025.

notices.short_title: CONDUENT CITYWIDE SI CLASS II Renewal #1
Identification, Inventorying, and Assessment of Parks Assets
notices.description:
NYC Parks seeks to better understand the complete inventory of assets on Parklands, to have them fully mapped on GIS along with relevant asset data and regularly inspected to identify their current state of repair and potential level of Capital need. The purpose of this request is to engage with Consultants to understand potential approaches and deliverables to more efficiently use funding and other resources to employ a needs assessment approach to the wider Parks portfolio. This will enable NYC Parks to better plan and budget for its capital plans in the future. NYC Parks invites interested Consultants who have experience with developing such inventorying and inspection programs for Owners of large asset portfolios to express their interest by responding to this RFEI. Interested consultants may obtain the full RFEI document by searching for EPIN: 84626Y0534 in PASSPort, and submitting a response to rfpsubmissions@parks.nyc.gov no later than June 26, 2026, at 2:00PM.

notices.short_title: JUNE 11, 2026 PUBLIC HEARING
notices.description:
NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN THAT THE NEW YORK CITY RENT GUIDELINES BOARD (RGB) will hold a public hearing on June 11, 2026 at The Theater at City Tech, NYC College of Technology, 285 Jay Street, Brooklyn, NY from 7:00 P.M. to 10:00 P.M to consider public comments concerning proposed rent adjustments on leases for apartments, lofts, hotels (including class A and class B hotels, SROs, rooming houses and lodging houses) and other housing units subject to the Rent Stabilization Law of 1969 and the Emergency Tenant Protection Act of 1974. These adjustments will affect leases commencing between October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2027. 

Proposed rent guidelines for all of the above classes of stabilized housing units were adopted on May 7, 2026. Copies of the proposed guidelines are available from the NYC Rent Guidelines Board office at the above listed address, at the Boards website nyc.gov/rgb, or at rules.cityofnewyork.us.
